qcPhotosArticle.title: Kakobuy QC Photos: Find, Check and Request Better Pictures
qcPhotosArticle.lede: Find the right warehouse photos, compare them with your exact order and request the one missing view that could change your decision. Includes a practical clothing and shoe inspection workflow.
sections: Find photos that belong to your order

Kakobuy QC photos are warehouse inspection pictures associated with a received item. Start from the order or warehouse record in your account and identify the item by its order reference, selected size, color and quantity. The interface may change, so follow the inspection or photo area attached to that record rather than relying on a button name from an old tutorial. Save the source listing and option image beside the warehouse views. You need two separate records: what you ordered and what the warehouse actually photographed.

A seller image, a spreadsheet thumbnail and another buyer’s QC picture can all help you recognize a product, but none establishes the condition of your own item. Check that every photo you review belongs to the same received unit. If several similar products arrived together, compare their order references before drawing conclusions. An apparently wrong color can be a record mix-up; an apparently perfect public QC album can belong to an entirely different size or batch.
When QC pictures are missing or will not load

First distinguish an item still travelling to the warehouse from an item marked received with an empty photo area. Seller dispatch, warehouse arrival, inspection and photo availability are separate events. A transport update does not prove that inspection is finished. Reopen the order record, check its current stage and try the supported app or website again. Do not accept an item simply because the interface shows no visible problem when the evidence itself is missing.

If the record should contain photos but they remain unavailable, send support the order reference, the affected image area and the time of your last check. Describe the display problem separately from any suspected product defect. Ask whether inspection is complete and how to obtain the images needed for your decision. Keep an eye on the actual after-sales deadline shown for the order: a missing picture should not be treated as an automatic extension of return eligibility.
Check identity before fine details

Read the size tag, compare the color option and count the pieces and included accessories. Match the item to the option you selected rather than to the main promotional picture, which may show a different bundle. For footwear, check both shoes and their size labels when visible. For a two-piece clothing set, confirm that both pieces appear. For accessories, look for straps, closures and small parts that the purchased option explicitly includes.

Write down observable differences. ‘Ordered navy, label and fabric appear black in two views’ is more useful than ‘wrong item’. Lighting can change perceived color, so ask for a neutral-light close-up if color is the only unresolved issue. Stop detailed inspection if the identity is clearly wrong: documenting the mismatch and requesting an eligible remedy is more useful than spending time evaluating stitching on an item you did not order.
Inspect clothes with a consistent measurement method

Use front and back views to locate stains, holes, uneven seams and misplaced prints. A folded garment can hide the lower hem or the back of a sleeve. If those areas matter, ask for them to be shown. Look at fasteners and embroidered details at a useful resolution; zooming a tiny compressed thumbnail cannot recover information that was never captured. Compare both sides before interpreting an apparent slant caused by how the garment lies on the table.

For fit, compare a measurement photo with a garment you already own, using the same method. A flat pit-to-pit width is not a body circumference. Specify the start and end points, whether the garment should lie relaxed, and the unit. For example, ask for a flat chest-width photo with the tape running straight from one underarm seam to the other. Do not infer a guaranteed fit from a size letter, a stretched tape or an angled photo.
Inspect shoes and accessories from useful angles

For shoes, compare toe shape, heel height, outsole alignment and the left/right pair in similar positions. Review stitching, obvious glue residue, separated edges and visible damage. A wide-angle lens can exaggerate the closer shoe, so apparent asymmetry deserves a second matched view before rejection. A size tag records the labelled size; it does not verify internal comfort or the shape of the last. Ask for an appropriate measurement only if it will meaningfully inform your decision.

For a bag or other accessory, inspect corners, edge finish, strap attachment points, closures and the included hardware. Ask for the clasp or zip area to be shown if an open/closed state is relevant. Still photography cannot establish long-term wear, material composition, authenticity or safe electrical function. Treat an untested function as unknown. Avoid translating ‘no visible defect in these photos’ into a broader quality guarantee.
Request a specific extra photo

An effective request names the item, the location and the decision it supports. For example: ‘For this order, please photograph the right shoe’s outer heel seam close enough to see whether the edge is separated.’ A measurement request might read: ‘Please show the jacket lying flat with a ruler across the chest, underarm seam to underarm seam, in centimetres.’ These are illustrative instructions, not promises that every service is available or free.

Check the current price, availability and processing conditions before ordering extra photography. Prefer one or two decisive views over a long list of general beauty shots. If you suspect a specific defect, identify it on the existing photo without covering the relevant area. Keep your wording factual and concise. A warehouse employee can act on a clearly located seam or missing measurement more easily than on a request to ‘check if everything is perfect’.
Choose accept, investigate or request after-sales

Accept when the recorded variant matches, the required views are present and the remaining uncertainty is acceptable to you. Request more evidence when a missing angle or measurement could change that conclusion. Raise an after-sales request when you can document a meaningful mismatch or visible defect and the order remains eligible. Keep the original order information, the relevant photos and your explanation together so the issue can be understood without reconstructing your browsing history.

Storage allowance and return eligibility are separate. Check the applicable deadline, seller conditions and any domestic return charge before waiting for more items to arrive. Avoid removing labels or requesting irreversible alterations until you have accepted the product. A longer warehouse storage period does not extend the seller’s return window, and a submitted international parcel may make an ordinary warehouse return impractical.
Keep a useful QC record for the next purchase

Record the inspection date, ordered option, observed measurements, unresolved limitations and final decision. Keep private order references out of any public album. If you share an example, say which views you inspected and what the photos cannot establish. That produces a more useful review than a simple approval score. After acceptance, move to parcel planning: the item’s inspection weight and its final packed shipping weight may differ, especially when protective packaging is added.

feesArticle.title: Kakobuy Fees and Total Cost: Build a Complete Order Budget
feesArticle.lede: Separate product payment, domestic delivery, payment charges, optional services and international shipping. Use a worked budget to compare the full cost without assuming fixed Kakobuy fees.
sections: Start with the two payment stages

A Kakobuy order budget normally needs at least two checkpoints: buying the item and submitting the international parcel. The seller’s product price is not the delivered price to your address. Between those checkpoints, domestic transport, warehouse services, payment conversion and the final packed parcel can change your total. Keep each cost in a separate line so a low headline product price does not hide a more expensive delivery decision.

This guide provides a budgeting method, not a current Kakobuy tariff. Payment methods, currency conversion, optional services and routes can change. Use the amounts displayed for your own order and selected payment method. If a line is unknown, mark it as unknown and keep a reserve; entering zero makes an incomplete estimate look more precise than it is. Save the date and currency alongside every quote you use.
Record product cost and domestic shipping

Multiply the price of the exact selected variant by the quantity. A listing may show a starting price for its cheapest option, while your selected size, material or bundle costs more. Confirm the actual cart line after selecting the variant. Record seller-to-warehouse delivery separately. Two products from the same seller do not automatically qualify for combined domestic shipping, and products from different sellers may arrive in separate deliveries.

Keep discounts distinct from costs. Note whether a reduction applies to the item, the domestic delivery or a later international parcel, and whether it requires a minimum amount. Do not subtract a promotional coupon from the whole budget until the relevant checkout accepts it. If one product becomes unavailable, recalculate the rest of the order rather than assuming a bundle price or shipping reduction still applies.
Compare payment charges and currency conversion

Look at both the credited balance and the amount your payment account is charged. A payment-channel fee and an exchange-rate difference are separate sources of cost. A method advertising a low percentage can still produce a higher final amount if its conversion is less favorable for your currency. Compare the complete payable amount for the same credit or purchase, at approximately the same time, before choosing between available methods.

Use a consistent accounting basis. You can track the platform’s item and service costs in CNY, then convert the subtotal using your actual payment result. Alternatively, record the final amount charged in your home currency and allocate it once. Do not add a separate conversion allowance if it is already included in that charged total. This double counting is a common reason a spreadsheet budget no longer matches the payment statement.
Add only the services you actually select

Extra photographs, measurements, packing changes, reinforcement or other warehouse services may appear as separate options. Read the current description and price for each before selecting it. Some services are useful only for a specific decision: a chest measurement may resolve a fit concern, while another general photo adds little. Record the purpose of the service so you can decide whether its cost is justified by the uncertainty it removes.

Return and exchange costs belong in a separate contingency line until they are known. Seller eligibility, domestic return transport, replacement availability and payment adjustments can affect the outcome. Do not assume that a return request makes every earlier cost refundable. Keep refundable and nonrefundable amounts separate and reconcile the actual adjustment after the case closes. A refund credit is not the same thing as a completed transfer back to your payment account.
Estimate freight from the parcel, not just the products

International shipping depends on destination, available route, item restrictions and packed measurements. An item’s warehouse weight is useful input, but it is not necessarily the final billed parcel weight. Boxes, protective material and consolidation change both mass and dimensions. Some routes compare actual with volumetric weight, while others have specific thresholds or rounding rules. Read the selected route’s conditions instead of assuming one universal formula applies.

Use the shipping page’s billable-weight calculator to explore how dimensions affect the weight estimate. Enter the divisor from your route; the calculator does not return a live freight price. Then compare current quotes for the same destination, contents and packing assumptions. Record what is included, what remains conditional and when the quote was checked. A cheaper headline quote can be a poor comparison if it excludes an option included in the other.
A worked example with invented figures

Suppose your selected products total 300 CNY, domestic delivery is 20 CNY, the payment charge allocated to this purchase is 12 CNY, optional warehouse services are 15 CNY and the international freight estimate is 180 CNY. The planning subtotal is 527 CNY. These figures are deliberately illustrative: they are not a Kakobuy quote, a verified fee schedule or a prediction for a particular country. Replace every amount with your current checkout information.

If the final freight amount becomes 210 CNY, the revised subtotal is 557 CNY, an increase of 30 CNY. Add any destination charge that actually applies and has not already been included. If the 12 CNY payment charge was already built into the amount you recorded as paid, remove it from the separate line. The point of the example is to make every change traceable, rather than to promise a fixed percentage for all purchases.
Compare consolidation using two complete scenarios

Create one budget for a combined parcel and another for the proposed smaller parcels. Include all repeated packaging, service charges and route minimums shown by the estimator. Compare realistic packed dimensions, not the sum of item weights alone. Combining orders may reduce repeated packaging, but a large box can also increase volumetric weight or remove a route from the available list. Neither option is automatically cheaper.

Keep customs information accurate and check the rules that apply to the destination through the appropriate official source before shipping. A route label is not a blanket exemption from all charges or restrictions. This article does not calculate duties or tax eligibility. In your budget, mark whether those amounts are included, excluded or still unknown according to the current route terms and destination requirements.
Close the budget after the parcel is billed

Keep three columns: estimated, actually paid and still unresolved. Reconcile the product payment, service charges, final freight, adjustments and any applicable destination amount. Save enough detail to explain the difference without publishing private order or payment identifiers. For a future purchase, reuse the structure and your packing experience, then refresh every variable price. Your previous parcel is a useful planning example, not a permanent Kakobuy shipping rate.

linksArticle.title: Kakobuy Links: Use Taobao and Weidian Product URLs
linksArticle.lede: Turn a Taobao or Weidian listing into a traceable Kakobuy order. Learn what to check after importing a link and how to diagnose short links, unavailable items and mismatched variants.
sections: Distinguish a source link from a shopping-agent link

A Taobao or Weidian source URL identifies a marketplace listing. A Kakobuy item URL opens an agent’s representation of that listing. A spreadsheet or discovery page may link to either one or to an intermediate catalog. Before pasting anything into an order flow, establish which type you have and what actual product it refers to. The text printed on a link can differ from its destination, so inspect the address reached after opening it.

Keep the source listing as your reference whenever it is available. Record the marketplace, product identifier, seller, selected variant and date. An agent page can simplify the ordering interface, but it does not eliminate the need to compare the underlying product. A ‘link converter’ should preserve the product identity; it cannot guarantee stock, seller reliability, return eligibility or that every marketplace option will import correctly.
Copy the complete product URL

Open the specific listing rather than the seller’s homepage, a search-results page or a cart. Use the marketplace’s share or copy-link function when available, then check the resulting address. A share message may contain promotional text around the URL. Paste the product address itself into the supported Kakobuy search or ordering field. Interface labels and supported marketplace formats can change, so use the current instructions shown by the platform.

For a short link, open it through the normal marketplace interface and confirm the final listing before using it. Do not replace the seller or product identifier by guessing from a similar-looking URL. Retain any parameters necessary to identify the product, while avoiding the public sharing of account-specific or session information. A screenshot of a link is not a substitute for the actual address and can introduce transcription errors.
Check the imported item before choosing options

After the item loads, compare its title, seller context, main images and source product identifier with the original. A translated title may be awkward but still describe the same item; a different product or seller is a more serious mismatch. Check more than the hero image because one promotional image can be reused across several listings. Confirm that the option images belong to the same record and that the listing is still available.

Next select the color, size, quantity and any bundle or material option. Recheck the payable line after selection, since the price displayed before choosing a variant may be only a starting price. If a translated option is ambiguous, compare its original text and thumbnail rather than choosing the closest English word. Save the exact option you selected so the warehouse QC review later has a reliable reference.
When a link does not load

Classify the failure before trying another purchase route. The URL may be incomplete, the short link may not have resolved, the listing may require a normal marketplace login, the seller may have removed the product, or the current agent interface may not support that format. Check whether the original listing still opens for you through the marketplace’s normal access flow. An import failure alone does not prove that the seller has disappeared.

If the source opens but import fails, use any manual-order or support option that the current platform actually provides. Supply the source URL, a clear product description and the required variant; do not invent an agent URL or assume an unsupported item can be purchased. If the original listing is unavailable, search for a replacement as a new candidate. Recheck seller, options and terms from the beginning, even if the photos look identical.
Use a spreadsheet as a shortlist, then verify

A useful Kakobuy links spreadsheet records what was found and when, rather than implying that every entry is permanently in stock. Keep columns for source URL, marketplace, seller, selected variant, listed price, inspection status and last check. Separate seller images from warehouse photos. If the sheet includes public QC examples, record that they belong to another purchase and may not show the item you will receive.

Before ordering from an old row, open the live destination again. A price can change, a seller can revise options and a product page can be repurposed. Mark unavailable entries instead of silently replacing them with a different item under the same name. If you share a replacement, give it its own record and date. This simple distinction prevents a collection of links from becoming an untraceable set of substitutions.
An example: a jacket with several options

Imagine a jacket listing with two fabrics, five colors and a size range. The spreadsheet thumbnail shows the padded version, while the lowest displayed price belongs to the unpadded version. After importing the URL, choosing ‘black’ alone is not enough: you must also select the intended fabric and size. Compare the final price and option image before paying. This is an illustrative scenario, not a claim about a particular seller or live product.

Save the chosen fabric description, the color thumbnail and the size chart with the order record. When QC photos arrive, check the tag, color and visible construction against that record. If warmth or material composition is decisive, remember that a photo cannot verify those properties by itself. A successful link import only gets the product into the order workflow; it does not resolve every uncertainty about the item.
Keep the catalog and the checkout distinct

Kakobuy VIP is an independent guide, not the shopping agent. Product search and listing cards can open an external discovery catalog. That page may help you locate a source, but it is not proof that you are logged into Kakobuy or ready to pay for a verified order. Check the complete destination domain and the relevant order record before entering account or payment information. A familiar logo alone does not establish who operates the page.

Never give a third-party converter your account password or payment details merely to rewrite a product URL. A tool that only needs to transform a public listing address should not need those secrets. If a route becomes confusing, return to your known account entry point and reconstruct the order from the original source. Keep private order references out of publicly shared spreadsheets and screenshots.
Finish with an order record that survives changes

Store the source URL, selected options, price context, date and any seller condition that affected your decision. After arrival, add your own QC observations; after shipping, add the packed measurements and actual cost. This creates a useful history even if the original link later stops working. For the next purchase, use that history as a starting point and verify the current listing again. A working URL is a research input, not an endorsement of the product.

trackingArticle.title: Kakobuy Tracking: Order Stages, Parcel Updates and Delays
trackingArticle.lede: Separate seller delivery, warehouse processing, international transport and the final carrier. Learn what a missing scan means and what information to collect before asking for help.
sections: Identify the shipment you are tracking

A Kakobuy purchase can involve a seller-to-warehouse delivery and a later international parcel. These are different movements and may use different tracking numbers. Start by asking where the item is supposed to be going at the current stage. A domestic seller number normally describes travel to the warehouse, while the parcel record created for international dispatch describes the consolidated shipment. Do not expect one number to explain every stage from purchase to your front door.

Keep a simple timeline with the order reference, seller dispatch date when available, warehouse receipt, inspection completion, parcel submission and the latest carrier scan. Save the original status wording and its time zone. Translating every status into ‘shipped’ loses the distinction between preparation, handover and physical movement. A timeline also makes it easier to identify whether the unresolved step belongs to the seller, the warehouse or the transport route.
Read the order stage before the tracking number

An item still being purchased or prepared by the seller is not yet an international parcel. If the order is waiting for domestic dispatch, look at the seller-stage information and any message about stock or required options. If domestic tracking says delivered, check whether the warehouse record has been matched and processed. A carrier’s delivery scan and the appearance of inspection photos do not necessarily happen at the same moment.

Once the item is available in the warehouse, inspect it before selecting parcel services. A submitted parcel may still be waiting for packing, measurement, payment adjustment or collection. Read the current parcel-stage message instead of assuming that submission equals departure. When an action is requested from you, such as confirming an option or resolving a payment difference, waiting for a carrier update will not complete that action.
A tracking number is not the same as a pickup scan

A label or electronic shipment record can exist before a carrier physically receives the parcel. Statuses such as information received or label created should therefore be read literally. They indicate a record, not necessarily transport. Check the route description for how tracking is published, because some routes expose an intermediate movement differently from the final delivery carrier. Avoid inferring the parcel’s exact location from an empty tracking page.

Recheck through the tracking information attached to the parcel record and the identified carrier’s normal tracking service. Use the correct number for that leg of the journey. If a new local number appears after a handover, keep both numbers in your timeline. Do not assume that a website accepting the number has independently confirmed the shipment; the useful evidence is the dated event and the carrier or route responsible for it.
Interpret gaps and handovers carefully

International transport can include periods without a public scan. A gap does not by itself prove loss, customs seizure or delivery. Compare the last event with the current route’s stated tracking behavior and delivery estimate. Look for an explicit exception, failed delivery attempt, request for information or address issue. Those actionable messages deserve attention even when the overall transit time still falls within the estimate.

A final-mile handover can produce different wording or timestamps between systems. Save the latest events from each relevant record without adding them together as if they were separate journeys. If one carrier says received and another has only electronic information, ask which physical handover is confirmed. This is more precise than assuming that the most optimistic estimated arrival date is authoritative.
Treat shipping time as a sequence, not one promise

Total time from purchase to delivery includes seller processing, domestic travel, warehouse work, your own inspection and decisions, parcel preparation, international transport and final delivery. A freight estimate may refer only to part of that sequence. Note the stated start point and whether the estimate uses business or calendar days. It is not a reliable comparison to measure one buyer’s payment-to-door experience against another route’s carrier-only estimate.

Do not choose a universal number of days from an old review. Destination, route availability, contents and operational conditions can change. For a date-sensitive purchase, compare the current estimate with every earlier stage that still has to happen and allow for unresolved steps. This guide does not promise a delivery date or publish an unverified country-by-country timetable. Your active parcel record is the place to check the current estimate.
Send support a concise evidence packet

When a shipment is outside its stated window, has an explicit exception or requires clarification, collect the parcel reference, relevant tracking number, route, destination country, latest event and the date you checked. Include a screenshot if the wording is unclear, but remove private information from anything shared publicly. Explain the discrepancy: for example, the parcel record says handed over while the carrier still shows only electronic information.

Ask a question that identifies the next action: whether physical collection is confirmed, whether another tracking number applies, whether information is required from you, or which investigation process is available. Do not request a guaranteed delivery date that the evidence cannot support. Keep the reply and any case reference with the timeline, including the next date or condition the support team tells you to monitor.
Handle delivery exceptions using the current record

If tracking shows an address problem, attempted delivery or collection requirement, read the carrier’s actual instructions through its normal service. Check the destination details recorded in the order without publishing them. For a customs-related request, follow the current official procedure and provide accurate information; do not alter product values or descriptions to force an outcome. This guide does not replace destination-specific customs instructions.

If the status says delivered but the parcel is missing, check the stated delivery location and any available proof of delivery, then contact the responsible service promptly. Preserve packaging and visible damage evidence when a parcel does arrive with a problem. Compensation, insurance and claim deadlines depend on the applicable terms; a long delay alone does not establish the amount or availability of a refund.
Close the timeline with a useful delivery record

Record the actual arrival date and distinguish it from the purchase date, parcel submission date and first carrier scan. If you later publish a review, state the route, period and stages measured without exposing addresses or full tracking identifiers. That makes your experience understandable without turning one parcel into a universal shipping-time claim. Keep any unresolved damage or missing-item case separate from the fact that transport has ended.
